title: urnetwork / taskworker
description: Authenticated Taskworker deep dive. Task names come only from the finite registered target set; attribution is system or client without identity labels. Queue and aggregate exporter values are shown only with their owning fresh snapshot. Missing or stale telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: task submissions, finishes and failures / s
panels.description: Committed new task submissions and finished tasks across all scraped producer services in the selected env. Includes continuations and RunOnce successors. Rollbacks are excluded from submitted/finished; completion may leave a durable post retry. Function failures count returned errors before retry writes or finalization. Finalization failures separately count each participating task in a failed handback invocation, including unknown commit replies; a function may have succeeded. These populations overlap and must not be summed. Repeated attempts count again; these are not distinct tasks or financial commits. Graceful drain (cause=drained) is excluded from function failures; other cancellations remain failures. Rates per second use $__rate_interval. Host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: function failures by target / s
panels.description: Failed function attempts per finite registered target (task label = package.function) across all scraped producer services in the selected env, summed over caller attribution and typed causes. Uses the same function-failure scope as the adjacent total: graceful drain (cause=drained) is excluded; other cancellations remain failures. Repeated failures count again; missing targets appear as unregistered. This counts function outcomes before retry writes or finalization, not committed task or financial work. Rates per second use $__rate_interval. Host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: finalization failures by target, phase and cause / s
panels.description: Failed finalization invocations per participating task by finite registered target, source phase and typed cause. Count each distinct member once in a failed batch or cohort; safe single fallback is a new attempt and delegation is counted once. Pre-transaction compatibility fallback is excluded. The phase marks the operation entered before terminal failure, not necessarily the first causal fault; a returned Post error followed by an aborted-transaction write appears at queue_update. Acquire does not identify Ping versus pool capacity; admission is pre-BEGIN business ownership. Includes unknown commit replies: the commit may have succeeded. Acknowledged identifies a failure observed after confirmed commit, not rollback. External task-post results are outside this counter. Older binaries may have the aggregate failure counter without phase telemetry. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero. Host/block filters do not apply.

panels.title: ready workers
panels.description: Instances whose startup readiness latch is set; this does not prove current task execution or finalization progress.

panels.title: executions in flight
panels.description: Registered task functions currently running, across system and client-attributed work.

panels.title: fresh available queue depth
panels.description: Maximum replica observation of available rows from one database snapshot, shown only while the snapshot is under 45 seconds old. Exact up to 10,000 available rows; past that a planner estimate, flagged in fresh queue depth by state.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!="",state="available"} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: fresh oldest overdue task
panels.description: Seconds past run_at for the oldest available row, only from a fresh bounded queue snapshot. The snapshot reads the first 10,000 available rows in poll order, which is every available row unless the available depth is estimated.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_taskworker_queue_oldest_overdue_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: task executions by outcome
panels.description: Execution starts and bounded terminal outcomes per finite registered task.

panels.title: system vs client-attributed executions
panels.description: Task metadata distinguishes system work from client-attributed work without retaining a client identity label.

panels.title: mean execution duration
panels.description: Rate-derived mean function duration per registered task and attribution.

targets.expr: sum by (task, attribution) (rate(urnetwork_taskworker_execution_duration_seconds_sum{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (task, attribution) (rate(urnetwork_taskworker_execution_duration_seconds_count{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: fresh one-minute maximum execution duration
panels.description: Exact process maxima only while the owning completion is under 120 seconds old; idle tasks remain no-data.

targets.expr: max by (task, attribution) (urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance, task, attribution) (urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: tasks balked / s (RunOnce conflicts)
panels.description: RunOnce conflicts across all scraped producer services in the selected env, including accepted coalescing and IfAbsent refusals. An active conflict may still request a later run. Rolled-back attempts are excluded; host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: task argument and result bytes / s
panels.description: Serialized input and already-produced output bytes; payload contents and identities are never labels.

panels.title: fresh queue depth by state
panels.description: Database-wide total, available, claimed, and reschedule_error states. Max across replicas avoids multiplying the shared queue; samples expire after 45 seconds. Each side of the availability boundary is counted exactly up to 10,000 rows; past that a state is a planner estimate, and claimed a lower bound, shown as 1 by its estimated series on the right axis.

targets.expr: max by (state) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

max by (state) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth_estimated{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: poll and queue snapshot pressure
panels.description: EvalTasks claim/empty/error outcomes plus bounded queue snapshot failures.

panels.title: finalization and reschedule outcomes
panels.description: Acknowledged completion, reschedule and post-hook reschedule outcomes after task execution. Failed or unacknowledged finalization attempts are shown separately at the top. External post errors are not counted here.

panels.title: lease refresh failures
panels.description: Task timestamp lease refresh errors; these can strand claimed work and deserve separate visibility from function outcomes.

panels.title: drain and final handback
panels.description: Tasks in flight at drain start, tasks canceled and rescheduled, and drain duration. The runner flushes metrics after final handback.

panels.title: subscription aggregate exporter freshness
panels.description: Age of the freshest complete subscription snapshot. Values beyond 20 minutes are intentionally omitted by the subscriptions dashboard and §2.27 signal.

panels.title: egress probe fleet exporter
panels.description: Fresh completed provider-fleet snapshot controls; the dedicated egress board owns full outcome interpretation.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_attempt_providers{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 900 and urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_health_providers{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 900 and urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: Postgres and Redis pressure
panels.description: Initialized Postgres pool occupancy plus Redis connection and timeout controls.

panels.title: Postgres acquire and lifecycle pressure
panels.description: Acquire outcomes/wait and connection creation/destruction expose taskworker database saturation.

panels.title: process CPU, memory, and goroutines
panels.description: Taskworker process saturation controls by selected deploy block and host.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores active phase spans
panels.description: Current spans by worker and phase. target_export is the parent of target_map, gob_encode, and cache_write. Parallel work can activate several spans; do not sum parent and child phases.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores completed phase wall time / s
panels.description: Wall seconds accumulated by completed spans per second. Concurrent spans can exceed one second per second, and target_export includes child phases. This measures wall time, not CPU time; active spans contribute only when they exit.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase exits / s
panels.description: Phase exits per second including error and panic cleanup. An exit does not imply success; rates describe distinct phase lifecycles.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase work items / s
panels.description: Work units per second: source_load rows, target_export passes, target_map/filter inputs inspected, gob_encode values, and cache_write Redis SET attempts. Units differ by phase, and retries contribute additional attempts.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase workload bytes / s
panels.description: Bytes produced by gob_encode or submitted as Redis key and value bytes in cache_write SET attempts, including retries. Other phases are zero. These are workload bytes, not heap allocations or confirmed Redis writes.

panels.title: failed finalization mean elapsed by phase
panels.description: Mean whole failed-invocation wall time including rollback and cleanup, grouped by entered source phase. One latency observation per finalizer invocation; a shared batch/cohort is one observation while its error counter counts participating tasks. This is not phase-only time, SQL runtime, or financial rollback latency. No successful attempts are included. External task-post joins after finalizer return are outside this measurement. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero. Host/block filters do not apply.

panels.title: payer debits, payout sweeps and finalization admission
payer debit batches / s by result
panels.description: Asynchronous payer debit batches by result; not contract throughput or provider payout.

panels.title: debit worker owners by shard
panels.description: Current bounded debit worker owners by partition and reporting process.

panels.title: oldest retained debit by shard
panels.description: Oldest retained debit age by worker partition, including committed records awaiting their Redis release.

panels.title: debit worker observation and completion age
panels.description: Time since the last successful oldest-debit observation (including empty partitions) and since the last debit-worker completion without a failed balance. Busy balances can remain pending after a completion.

panels.title: payout sweep assignment statements
panels.description: Assignment statements running now and the rows they selected (not rows updated or committed), and the mean rows selected per attempt including retries and dry runs.

panels.title: payout sweep assignment mean residence
panels.description: Statement residence through row-count validation by outcome, from the histogram sum and count. matched is not a transaction commit; error includes panic.

panels.title: finalization admission errors and skipped lease refreshes / s
panels.description: Failed finalization admission attempts per participating task by entered stage and cause (an acknowledged busy wait does not prove one continuous wait), and task timestamp hints skipped because ownership was busy or the claim no longer matched.

panels.title: account outbox deliveries and payout wallet sources / s
panels.description: Account message outbox deliveries by template and result, and release payout providers by the source that selected their wallet, or why none was selected.

panels.title: claims handed back to a newer config / s
panels.description: URL probe passes, disabled markers, contract degradation checks and verification chains that a taskworker claimed and handed back unchanged, because a newer config's live stamp owns them, by task family. A steady rate means taskworkers on an older config run beside a newer one: narrow the host to find them. Their claims cycle back to the newer config's instances until they restart on it.

panels.title: idle run-once chain wakes / s
panels.description: A recurring run-once chain that finds no work backs off to its idle delay and sets a wake mark in Redis (marked); once it runs at its active cadence again it removes its own mark (resumed). A producer in any service clears the marks of the chains its committed work feeds: active, the chain had no mark (one Redis round trip, no queue write); kicked, this producer removed the mark and pulled the chain's pending row to now; busy, the chain's queue key was held, so its holder reads the new work; due, the row was already due. error: a mark, clear or kick that failed; the chain still runs at its idle delay. Producers run in every service, so the host and block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: client location reliability pass: clients and rows written
panels.description: What the last client location reliability pass (UpdateClientLocationReliabilities) each taskworker ran computed: its clients by identity kind (hosted_child, a hosted child identity with source_client_id set, which most readers exclude; top_level, the rest), and the rows its upsert inserted or rewrote. A connected client's row is rewritten only when a value changed or once a day, so rows written far under the clients means the pass left unchanged rows alone. Each process keeps the numbers of the last pass it ran until it runs another; rows written is shown only for processes that have run a pass.

targets.expr: max by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_pass_written_rows{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) and on (host, block, instance) count by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_pass_clients{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""})

panels.title: points leaderboard: payments earning in payout weeks
panels.description: How approximate the last points leaderboard snapshot each taskworker published is (RebuildPointsLeaderboard, owner decision 2026-10-28). Blocks and Streak publish as soon as a completed operator block exists; a payment whose paid sweeps the history rollup has not measured earns in its payout weeks, every block from its oldest paid sweep to the end of its plan's traffic window, an upper bound of its measured blocks. rollup_pending payments are those, and stored rows replace their weeks as the rollup measures them; sweeps_reaped are completed payments the rollup measured after contract reaping had deleted their sweeps, whose weeks stay. rollup pending payments is the rollup's remaining work in any block; it should fall while the rebuild runs every minute. Each process keeps the numbers of the last rebuild it ran until it runs another.

panels.title: points leaderboard: approximate networks and unlinked points
panels.description: What the last points leaderboard snapshot each taskworker published counted: networks with a positive point among its payout-week or unlinked inputs, whose Blocks and Streak are approximate (never below their measured values), and positive post-genesis point rows without a payment row, each earning in the last block that closed before it posted. Unlinked points have no sweeps to measure; points-readiness warns while any exist. Each process keeps the numbers of the last rebuild it ran until it runs another.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot age
panels.description: Seconds since the newest SN Top snapshot (LEADERTOP.md) each taskworker computed or read was computed. A snapshot folds one tempo of about 72 minutes, a few minutes after it ends; the apps call the board stale past three tempos (about 3.6 hours). No data before the process saw a snapshot, or while st is disabled.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot counts
panels.description: What the newest SN Top snapshot each taskworker wrote counted, by kind: ranked networks, verify-eligible providers, measured providers (the verify cohort), claimed fleets (UIDs), open head seats and the non-seed hops of complete trails in the tempo. Counts only, no identities.

panels.title: SN Top board: Top 200 line and claimed floor
panels.description: The newest snapshot's projected 200th score (the Top 200 line every margin and label is measured from; 0 while fewer than 200 networks rank) and the floor among the claimed fleets the replica selects (no data without a claimed fleet).

panels.title: SN Top board: agreement with the validator and the chain
panels.description: Per folded tempo: UIDs whose replica score equals (match) or differs from (mismatch) the validator's exact head summary score, where any mismatch means the replica is wrong; and UIDs the validator selected that earn (earning) or do not earn (not_earning) on-chain incentive. All are 0 until fleets bind and the head summary and incentive reads arrive (LEADERTOP.md §6.3).

panels.title: SN Top board: precision at 200
panels.description: Of the claimed networks the previous snapshot projected inside the Top 200, the share the validator then selected. No data until fleets bind and a head summary arrives. The board's likely label turns on only at 0.9 or above (owner decision Q17); below that every row inside the line shows estimate.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot runs
panels.description: How long each taskworker's newest SN Top snapshot took to read its inputs, project and write, in seconds, and how many snapshots it wrote in the last hour (about one a tempo, 0.83 an hour). A process that checks but finds no completed tempo writes none.
